x: Pair A is wrong: no derivation of Telugu 'by all scholars exclusively from Tamil' is given; Telugu is said to have grown out of the Desi bhasha (Paisachi) of Prakrit, and its name is traced to Trilinga. The other pairs are correct: Trilinga refers to three Shaiva centres, Andhrika is another name of the language, and some derive Tenugu from tene (honey).

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Pre-Nannaya period runs to about 1000, and the Modern age runs from the 19th century onward. Statement 3 is false because only the Shiva Kavi Yugam (1060-1260) and the Errana age have firm boundaries; the other boundaries are approximate.

Krishna Satakam is an independent work of Tikkana, along with Nirvachanottara Ramayanam and Kavi Vakbandham. Kumarasambhavam is by Nannechoda, Basava Puranam by Palkuriki Somanatha, and Prataparudra Yashobhushanam by Vidyanatha.
Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita (the unity of Shiva and Vishnu; some notes say Harihara Dvaitam). He dedicated his Bharatam to Hariharanatha to reconcile Shaivas and Vaishnavas.

Ketana was called Abhinava Dandi for his Telugu Dasakumara Charitra, which he rendered from Dandin. In the other options the holders are wrong: Kavibrahma is Tikkana, Sambhudasa is Errana, and Kaviraja Sikhamani is Nannechoda.

Mahmud attacked Somnath in 1025, when the Solanki Bhima I ruled Gujarat. The other statements are wrong: the Pratihara king of Kanauj submitted to Mahmud and did not resist; Mahmud attacked Nagarkot in 1009, not Ghori in 1194; and Jaichand was the Gahadavala king of Kanauj whom Ghori defeated at Chandawar in 1194.
All three statements are correct. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir on the early Sultanate under the patronage of Qutbuddin Aibak, and Minhaj-us-Siraj dedicated Tabaqat-i-Nasiri to Nasiruddin Mahmud.

All three statements are correct. Nicolo Conti was a Venetian who described the innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara. The notes place him at the end of Deva Raya I's reign, but the APPSC 2011 key placed this Italian traveller in Deva Raya II's reign.

The notes credit Abdur Razzaq, the Timurid envoy to Deva Raya II's Vijayanagara, with mentioning '300 ports'. ⚠ The APPSC key said Barbosa, so recognise that answer if it appears in an APPSC paper. Nikitin was a Russian horse merchant, and Tavernier described the diamonds of Golconda.
key: Notes: '300 ports' was mentioned by Abdur Razzaq; the APPSC key's Barbosa is flagged as divergent
